name: JO-JOTTE
description: Jo-Jotte is a two-player trick-taking and melding game created by bridge expert Ely Culbertson in 1937. It is a sophisticated hybrid that combines the bidding and scoring philosophies of Contract Bridge with the card-ranking and melding mechanics of Belote and Klaberjass. Named after his wife Josephine, it was marketed as the ultimate two-player intellectual card game.

content.text: Jo-Jotte is a two-player trick-taking and melding game created by bridge expert Ely Culbertson in 1937. It is a sophisticated hybrid that combines the bidding and scoring philosophies of Contract Bridge with the card-ranking and melding mechanics of Belote and Klaberjass. Named after his wife Josephine, it was marketed as the ultimate two-player intellectual card game.
Invented by Ely Culbertson, who sought a two-player game with the strategic depth of Bridge. He drew heavily from the European game Klaberjass (Clobyosh).
Two players. The first dealer is determined by a single cut of the deck (low card deals first). Thereafter the deal alternates between the two players.
Deal six cards to each player. One card is turned up to start the bidding. After trump is set, three more cards are dealt to each player (total of 9 cards).
